"88863802-911c-559b-a7a4-c6fd80ee55d9" :question/problem "There are currently $498$ koalas living in a secluded forest, but their population is decreasing at a continuously compounded rate of $3.4\%$ per year. How many years must pass for there to be only $12$ koalas left in that forest? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question."] [:db/add "88863802-911c-559b-a7a4-c6fd80ee55d9" :question/worked-solution "The initial population is $P_0=498$ and the final population is $P=12$. A decrease of $3.4\%$ per year means $r=-0.034$, with $t$ in years.

Use the continuously compounded growth equation, isolate the exponential, take natural logarithms, and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P &= P_0e^{rt} \\
12 &= 498e^{-0.034t} \\
e^{-0.034t} &= \frac{12}{498} \\
\ln\left(e^{-0.034t}\right) &= \ln\left(\frac{12}{498}\right) \\
-0.034t &= \ln\left(\frac{12}{498}\right) \\
t &= \frac{\ln\left(\frac{12}{498}\right)}{-0.034} \\
t &\approx 109.57922 \\
t &\approx 110\text{ years}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time is approximately $110$ years."] [:db/add "88863802-911c-559b-a7a4-c6fd80ee55d9" :question/requires-calculator true] [:db/add "88863802-911c-559b-a7a4-c6fd80ee55d9"
